c.tagline: Thailand's laid-back northern capital of golden temples, misty mountains, and digital nomads.

taxi.fareNote: Red songthaew shared trucks are the everyday local taxi — flag one down, state your destination, and expect about 30-60 baht per person for short hops agreed before you ride; tuk-tuks and Grab/Bolt are the easy alternatives, as metered street taxis are scarce.

emergency.note: Tourist Police 1155 has English-speaking operators; 191 reaches police and 1669 the ambulance/medical service.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Riverside (Wat Ket): Ping River Wat Ket, Chiang Mai
hood_landmark.Night Bazaar (Chang Khlan): Chiang Mai Night Bazaar, Chang Khlan

avoid.reason: Scooter rental-damage scams and road-accident risk; heavy smoke/haze Mar–Apr

hood_desc: The moat-ringed historic heart, packed with centuries-old temples like Wat Phra Singh and Wat Chedi Luang and lined with quiet lanes, guesthouses, and cafes; the classic base for first-time visitors who want everything walkable.

Chiang Mai's trendy west-side district of hip cafes, art galleries, wine bars, co-working spaces, and boutiques near Chiang Mai University; the hub for digital nomads and a younger, design-conscious crowd.
The leafy east bank of the Ping River around Wat Ket, lined with old teak houses, riverside restaurants, and five-star resorts; a relaxed, scenic area for slower stays.
An up-and-coming local neighborhood just north of the Old City between it and Nimman, full of fresh markets, cheap eats, and affordable rooms; a favorite of budget travelers and long-stay expats.
The commercial strip east of the Old City built around the sprawling nightly Night Bazaar on Chang Khlan Road, with big hotels, massage parlors, bars, and shopping; lively and central but touristy.
lodging: Ibis Styles Chiang Mai Night Bazaar

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water rather than tap.

transit.pay: Pay songthaews and tuk-tuks in cash directly to the driver — around 30-60 baht per person for short hops, agreed before you ride; RTC city buses cost about 30 baht flat (cash or QR). There is no rechargeable transit card system.
transit.hours: Red songthaews and tuk-tuks run informally through the day and into the night; the RTC city bus network runs roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM, with Grab and Bolt filling the late-night gap.
transit.note: Chiang Mai has no metro, tram, or urban rail; getting around means red songthaew shared trucks (the local workhorse), a small RTC city bus network, tuk-tuks, and ride-hailing apps.

bus: Arcade (Chang Phueak) bus terminal for intercity coaches to Bangkok, Chiang Rai, and Pai

car.idp: Required (International Driving Permit needed alongside your home license)

train: Chiang Mai Railway Station (State Railway of Thailand line to Bangkok via Phitsanulok and Ayutthaya)

transit.m: RTC airport shuttle bus to the Old City / Night Bazaar (~20-30 min)
Airport flat-rate taxi to the city center (150-200 baht, 15-25 min)

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up the bill or leaving 20-40 baht for good service at restaurants is appreciated but not required.
